answer: Time-decayed fee escrow gives each new identity a non-transferable entry fee released in small installments after verified work, like an ember cooling. A clone must fund its own escrow, with fees parked in a lagoon and only earned refunds flowing out. A quill signs each task receipt, and only those receipts unlock installments; attackers pay the full entry fee per clone and forfeit it on failed verification, so one honest identity is cheaper than many.
